newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-CSKA MOSCOW PROMISE TO SETTLE DISPUTE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CSKA MOSCOW PROMISE TO SETTLE DISPUTE.

text.p: CSKA Moscow have told Russian soccer authorities they will meet a March 1 deadline to settle an internal row that has left two rival teams bidding for its premier league spot, a league official said on Friday.
The army club were told earlier this week to sort out the dispute by the deadline or risk having no league place when the 1997 season starts on March 15.

"We have received a letter from the CSKA sports club with assurances to settle the conflict on their own to meet the March 1 deadline," Boris Bobrov, the league's general director, told Reuters by telephone.

The row erupted when Alexander Baranovsky, chief of the Army Central Sports Club CSKA, sacked coach Alexander Tarkhanov at the end of last year and replaced him with former national team coach Pavel Sadyrin.
Baranovsky says the army controls 60 percent of the shares in the CSKA Moscow soccer club. But Tarkhanov says a businessman who backs him has a 68 percent majority and has refused to quit.
The Russian Football Union (RFS), which oversees all soccer in Russia, ruled in favour of Tarkhanov earlier this week but the dispute has raged on.
Most of the 1996 squad are training with Tarkhanov, who guided them to fifth place last season.
